answer: Seeded challenge custody: each new agent identity must solve a unique challenge derived from a rotating public entropy source and its own key. The nadir of a precomputed answer table is deep: because the seed changes per epoch, no answer is repeatable, so attackers cannot mass-replay solutions. A sable cipher commitment binds each submission to a single processor-second budget. Enforcement demands one fresh hardware-attested solve per identity, and the basalt-hard floor is that forging N identities costs N distinct hardware sessions plus N unshared compute proofs.
